propositions: fsck detects and classifies dirty tracker state into three kinds: tracked deletions restorable from HEAD, untracked regenerable compaction leftovers, and orphaned .tmp-event-* files, emitting distinct findings in both text and JSON output

doctor --repair heals dirty tracker wedges using two non-reentrant write-lock windows: window 1 restores deletions and quarantines leftovers under a scoped lock, window 2 releases the lock and invokes sync.reconverge for convergence
fsck JSON contract registers three new tracker-dirty kinds in _STRUCTURED_KINDS with per-class counts and paths, parsed losslessly via shlex quoting and declared-count boundaries

doctor repair actions record a backup ref at refs/rebar-doctor/<utc-ts> before any mutations, refuse all mutations if backup ref creation fails, and leave class-3 .tmp-event-* files untouched and byte-identical

Write lock is NOT held when reconverge is entered; it IS held during checkout/move steps; holding the lock across reconverge entry or mutating files outside the scoped window is forbidden by test assertion

doctor --repair on a clean store makes zero changes, creates no backup ref, and is idempotent; the file-mutating window respects existing lock semantics and never deletes files (only restores or quarantines)
